# FOR004 `function-result-component`

<Badge type="danger" text="error" /> <Badge type="tip" text="enabled by default" />

A component of a function result is referenced directly: `f(x)%c`.

## Why

Fortran does not allow a component (or a type-bound procedure) to be selected from a function
reference: `f(x)%c` is not a valid designator. Some compilers accept it as an extension, others
reject it or miscompile it. Assign the result to a variable, or use `associate (r => f(x))` and
then `r%c`.

## Reported

```fortran
n = grid_of(level)%ni
```

## Preferred

```fortran
associate (grid => grid_of(level))
  n = grid%ni
end associate
```

## Suppressing

For one occurrence, with the reason on the same line (or alone on the line before the statement):

```fortran
! fobis: ignore[FOR004] <why this occurrence is fine>
```

For the whole project, `ignore = FOR004` in the fobos [`[lint]` section](/fobos/lint).
